decisions.reason: Define-XML ADTTE.TRTDUR and native MT.ADTTE.TRTDUR explicitly name ADSL.TRTDUR, which is absent from the published ADSL columns. The ADSL ItemRef links TRTDURD to MT.ADSL.TRTDUR, but a method identifier does not establish an available TRTDUR variable.

Define-XML ADTTE.ADT says strictly after TRTSDT, and ADRG pages 11-12 justify consuming the published first treatment-emergent dermatologic event; the literal probe preserves those conditions and the RFENDTC conversion. The reported differences arise at the treatment-date boundary, while the inclusive and eligibility-before-selection readings have source support in ADAE.TRTEMFL and ADRG pages 11-12 respectively.

Define-XML ADSL.RFENDT explicitly states "RFENDTC converted to SAS date", so ADTTE.ADT names the raw text input and its conversion while ADTTE.SRCVAR names that converted date. Read with ADSL.RFENDT, these are compatible stages of the documented lineage rather than contradictory rules.

Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL selects an empty CQ01NAM, whereas ADRG pages 11-12 describe the first dermatologic event flag and ADAE.CQ01NAM names its populated value DERMATOLOGIC EVENTS. This is a genuine conflict in the upstream source-selection metadata, rather than a different SRCSEQ copy condition.

Define-XML ADTTE.STARTDT and native MT.ADTTE.STARTDT name ADSL.RFSTDTC, a text source, while adtte.yaml line 368 reads the distinct date variable ADSL.TRTSDT. Agreement of their values on this submission does not supply the documented source reference.

Define-XML ADTTE.ADT requires the selected event date to occur after TRTSDT. ADT first_available at adtte.yaml lines 386-390 accepts every nonmissing EVTSRC.ASTDT, and neither EVTSRC nor another ADT helper supplies that strict boundary.

Define-XML ADTTE.ADT always converts ADSL.RFENDTC on the fallback branch. EOS2DT at adtte.yaml lines 351-364 limits that source to deaths and otherwise uses the DS-derived EOSDT, introducing a different condition and source.

Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL selects TRTEMFL=Y records, and ADAE.TRTEMFL requires a nonmissing ASTDT at or after nonmissing TRTSDT; EVTSRC consumes that first-event flag. Within this documented source context, CNSR at adtte.yaml lines 408-410 tests existence of the same treatment-emergent event through its nonmissing date, so the finding treats an implied source condition as a separate divergence.

CNSR at adtte.yaml lines 408-410 is exactly zero when EVTSRC.ASTDT is nonmissing and one otherwise. Substituting that definition into Define-XML ADTTE.EVNTDESC gives the implemented conditions and both literal strings at lines 428-430, with no extra possible CNSR branch.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCDOM requires the domain actually supplying ADT, while the quoted strict boundary governs the upstream ADT calculation. ADT and SRCDOM at adtte.yaml lines 386-390 and 447-449 select their ADAE branch under the same nonmissing-event condition, so the missing ADT boundary is not an independent SRCDOM condition.
Define-XML ADTTE.SRCDOM requires the domain supplying ADT. In adtte.yaml, ADT can use EOSDT from DS_DISP.DSSTDTC through EOS2DT, but SRCDOM line 449 still labels that fallback ADSL.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCVAR requires the variable actually supplying ADT, while the quoted strict boundary governs the upstream ADT calculation. ADT at adtte.yaml lines 386-390 uses EVTSRC.ASTDT under the same nonmissing-event condition as SRCVAR line 466, so this finding propagates the ADT boundary issue into a separate source-label rule.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCVAR requires the variable supplying ADT, and ADSL.RFENDT documents the converted RFENDTC value. The non-death ADT fallback instead uses DS_DISP.DSSTDTC through EOSDT/EOS2DT, while SRCVAR at adtte.yaml line 468 still reports RFENDT.

SRCDOM at adtte.yaml lines 447-449 equals ADAE exactly when EVTSRC.ASTDT is nonmissing, which is the condition SRCSEQ uses at lines 485-486. Substituting that definition into Define-XML ADTTE.SRCSEQ gives the same AESEQ copy and otherwise missing result, so this is an equivalent expression of the documented predicate.

Native Define-XML IT.ADTTE.STUDYID has Origin Type="Predecessor" with the exact description "ADSL.STUDYID" at lines 1820-1824, corroborated by workbook Variables!M192 and P192. The ADTTE.STUDYID reading-copy section omits that Origin, but the retained native source documents the derivation.

Native Define-XML IT.ADTTE.USUBJID has Origin Type="Predecessor" with the exact description "ADSL.USUBJID" at lines 1838-1842, corroborated by workbook Variables!M194 and P194. The ADTTE.USUBJID reading-copy section omits that Origin, but the retained native source documents the derivation.

The retained sections, native workbook ADTTE.ADT method and native SDTM DS metadata do not state the exclusions or earliest-disposition selection in adtte.yaml DS_DISP. Define-XML ADTTE.ADT instead names ADSL.RFENDTC, whose upstream SDTM DM.RFENDTC comment refers to the last disposition event.

No retained section or native ADTTE method states month/day imputation for a DS-derived censor date. ADRG page 8 limits its partial-date instruction to ADAE.ASTDT, while Define-XML ADTTE.ADT states an RFENDTC conversion rather than the EOSDT imputation in adtte.yaml lines 345-349.

ADRG pages 11-12 describe treatment-emergent dermatologic first-event selection, and page 17 applies ADSL.SAFFL to the downstream KM analysis. Neither those sections nor the native ADTTE methods state the additional ADAE.SAFFL=Y source-event condition in EVTSRC at adtte.yaml line 56.

Define-XML ADTTE.CNSR tests TRTEMFL, and ADRG pages 11-12 describe its dermatologic first-event context. Page 17 applies safety-population selection downstream, but no retained source states the additional ADAE.SAFFL=Y event filter at adtte.yaml line 56 for CNSR.

ADRG pages 11-12 identify the first treatment-emergent dermatologic event and page 17 selects the downstream safety analysis population. No retained section or native SRCDOM method adds ADAE.SAFFL=Y when selecting the source event used by SRCDOM through EVTSRC at adtte.yaml line 56.

ADRG pages 11-12 identify the first treatment-emergent dermatologic event and page 17 selects the downstream safety analysis population. No retained section or native SRCVAR method adds ADAE.SAFFL=Y when selecting the source event used by SRCVAR through EVTSRC at adtte.yaml line 56.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCSEQ specifies AESEQ conditional on SRCDOM, and ADRG pages 11-12 describe the first treatment-emergent dermatologic source event. ADRG page 17 applies safety-population selection downstream, but no retained source adds the ADAE.SAFFL=Y event filter used for SRCSEQ through EVTSRC at adtte.yaml line 56.
